title: React Reference
description: A compact reference of the React 19 APIs, hooks, JSX rules and ecosystem commands used in the tutorial, grouped by topic, with syntax, a short example and the lesson that explains each entry.

entries.name: {expression}
entries.summary: Embeds any JavaScript expression inside JSX: variables, calls, arithmetic, ternaries. Statements such as if and for are not allowed.

entries.name: className
entries.summary: The JSX name for the HTML class attribute. for becomes htmlFor, and multi-word attributes are camelCase (tabIndex, onClick).
notes: Unknown lowercase names are passed through with a development warning

entries.name: style={{ … }}
entries.summary: Inline styles are an object with camelCase property names and string or number values.
notes: Unitless numbers become px for most properties

entries.name: <>…</> and <Fragment>
entries.summary: Groups several elements without adding a DOM node. Use the long form when the group needs a key, for example inside map.

entries.name: cond && <X /> and cond ? <A /> : <B />
entries.summary: Render conditionally with JavaScript operators. false, null, undefined and true render nothing; 0 and NaN render as text.
notes: Compare explicitly to avoid a stray 0: `items.length > 0 &&`
`return null` from a component renders nothing

entries.name: array.map with key
entries.summary: Renders a list by mapping data to elements. Every element needs a key that is unique among siblings and stable across renders.
notes: Do not use the index when the list can reorder or filter
`key` is not passed to the child as a prop

entries.name: createRoot(container).render(…)
entries.summary: Mounts a React tree into a DOM element; the entry point of every client-rendered app. Imported from react-dom/client.

entries.name: <StrictMode>
entries.summary: Development-only wrapper that renders components twice and runs effects twice to surface impure code and missing cleanups. It has no effect in production.

entries.name: function Component(props)
entries.summary: A component is a capitalized function that receives one props object and returns JSX or null. It must be pure during render.

entries.name: props
entries.summary: Attributes written on a component tag arrive as one object. Non-string values go in braces, a bare attribute is true, and defaults are set with destructuring.
entries.syntax: function Price({ amount, currency = 'EUR', onSale = false }) { … }
notes: Props are read-only; the parent owns the data
`defaultProps` is not supported on function components in React 19

entries.name: children
entries.summary: The content between a component's opening and closing tags, available as props.children; the basis of wrapper and layout components.

entries.name: memo(Component)
entries.summary: Returns a component that skips re-rendering when every prop is Object.is-equal to the previous render's props.
notes: Inline objects and functions defeat it; pair with useMemo and useCallback
The React Compiler makes manual memo mostly unnecessary

entries.name: lazy() and <Suspense>
entries.summary: lazy loads a component's module on first render; Suspense shows a fallback while it, or a promise read with use, is pending.

entries.name: useState(initial)
entries.summary: Declares a state variable and its setter. The initial value is used on the first render only; pass a function for lazy initialization.
notes: Setting state schedules a re-render; the variable changes on the next render
Replace objects and arrays instead of mutating them

entries.name: setState(prev => next)
entries.summary: Passing a function to the setter computes the next value from the latest state, so queued updates build on each other.

entries.name: useActionState(action, initialState)
entries.summary: React 19. Wraps an async form action and returns its latest result, a wrapped action for the form, and a pending flag.

entries.name: useFormStatus()
entries.summary: React 19, from react-dom. Reads the pending state of the enclosing form's action, typically inside a submit button component.

entries.name: useTransition()
entries.summary: Marks state updates as non-urgent so React keeps the UI responsive; in React 19 it also tracks async Actions outside forms.

entries.name: useDeferredValue(value)
entries.summary: Returns a copy of a value that lags behind during expensive renders, so typing stays smooth while a heavy list catches up.

entries.name: useEffect(setup, deps)
entries.summary: Runs setup after React commits to the DOM and re-runs it when a dependency changes. Use it to synchronize with things outside React.

entries.name: Effect cleanup
entries.summary: A function returned from the setup; React calls it before the next run and on unmount. Clear timers, remove listeners, abort requests, flip ignore flags.

entries.name: Dependency array
entries.summary: Omitted: the effect runs after every render. []: after the first render only. [a, b]: whenever a or b changes. List everything the effect reads.

entries.name: useRef(initial)
entries.summary: Returns a mutable object whose .current persists across renders; changing it never re-renders. Holds DOM nodes, timer ids and other non-rendered values.

entries.name: ref as a prop (React 19)
entries.summary: Function components receive ref as a normal prop and can forward it to an element; forwardRef is no longer needed.

entries.name: ref={node => …}
entries.summary: A function ref is called with the DOM node on mount; in React 19 it may return a cleanup that runs on unmount.

example.code:
<div
  ref={(node) => {
    const observer = new ResizeObserver(onResize);
    observer.observe(node);
    return () => observer.disconnect();
  }}
/>

entries.name: useImperativeHandle(ref, create)
entries.summary: Exposes a custom object (for example { focus }) through a ref instead of the raw DOM node. Rarely needed; forwarding the node is usually enough.

entries.name: createContext(defaultValue)
entries.summary: Creates a context object. The default is returned to readers that have no matching provider above them.

entries.name: <Context value={…}>
entries.summary: React 19 renders the context object itself as the provider; <Context.Provider> still works. Consumers re-render when value changes.
notes: Memoize object values with useMemo if consumers re-render too often

entries.name: useContext(Context)
entries.summary: Reads the nearest provider's value for the given context, or the default if there is none.

entries.name: use(resource)
entries.summary: React 19. Reads a context or a promise. Unlike other hooks it may be called conditionally; a pending promise suspends to the nearest Suspense boundary.
entries.syntax:
const settings = use(SettingsContext);
const data = use(cachedPromise);
notes: Promises must be stable across renders, never created during render

entries.name: Rules of hooks
entries.summary: Call hooks only at the top level of components or custom hooks, in the same order on every render, and never from plain functions. Enforced by eslint-plugin-react-hooks.

entries.name: function useSomething()
entries.summary: Any function that starts with use and calls hooks. It shares logic, not state: every call gets its own state.

entries.name: onClick={handler}
entries.summary: Event props are camelCase and take a function reference. Use an arrow function to pass arguments.
notes: `onClick={handler()}` calls the function during render instead of on click

entries.name: event (SyntheticEvent)
entries.summary: Handlers receive an event object with the DOM API: target, currentTarget, preventDefault(), stopPropagation().

entries.name: value + onChange
entries.summary: An input whose value comes from state and whose onChange writes back to it. Checkboxes use checked; select and textarea use value.

example.code:
const [name, setName] = useState('');

<input value={name} onChange={(e) => setName(e.target.value)} />

entries.name: <form action={fn}>
entries.summary: React 19. Passes the FormData to a function on submit; async functions become Actions with pending tracking and automatic reset of uncontrolled fields.

entries.name: new FormData(form)
entries.summary: Reads all named fields of a form at once; the natural fit for uncontrolled inputs and form Actions.

groups.title: Vite, React Router and TanStack Query

entries.name: npm create vite@latest
entries.summary: Scaffolds a project from a template; use --template react or react-ts. The -- forwards the option to create-vite.

entries.name: npm run dev
entries.summary: Starts the Vite development server with hot module replacement, by default at http://localhost:5173.

entries.name: npm run build / npm run preview
entries.summary: Builds the optimized static site into dist/ and, with preview, serves that folder locally for checking.

entries.name: <BrowserRouter>
entries.summary: Connects React Router to the browser URL; wrap the app once in main.jsx. Imported from the react-router package (version 7).

entries.name: <Routes> and <Route>
entries.summary: Routes picks the best matching Route by path and renders its element. path="*" catches unmatched URLs; index marks the parent's own path.

example.code:
<Routes>
  <Route element={<Layout />}>
    <Route index element={<Home />} />
    <Route path="products/:id" element={<Product />} />
    <Route path="*" element={<NotFound />} />
  </Route>
</Routes>

entries.name: <Link> and <NavLink>
entries.summary: Client-side navigation without a reload. NavLink additionally adds an active class and aria-current when its route matches.

entries.name: useParams()
entries.summary: Returns the dynamic segments of the current URL as strings, keyed by the names used in the route path.

entries.name: <Outlet />
entries.summary: Placeholder inside a layout route's element where the matched child route is rendered.

entries.name: useNavigate()
entries.summary: Returns a function for programmatic navigation: navigate('/path'), navigate(-1) to go back, or { replace: true } to replace the history entry.
entries.syntax:
const navigate = useNavigate();
navigate('/dashboard', { replace: true });

entries.name: QueryClientProvider
entries.summary: Provides a QueryClient, which holds the cache, to the component tree. Create one client at the root of the app.

entries.name: useQuery({ queryKey, queryFn })
entries.summary: Fetches and caches data by key; returns data, isPending, isError, error, isFetching and refetch. Components that share a key share one request and one cache entry.
notes: Put every variable the fetch depends on into the key
staleTime controls how long data counts as fresh

entries.name: useMutation({ mutationFn })
entries.summary: Wraps a write operation with pending and error state; call invalidateQueries in onSuccess to refetch the lists it affects.
